title: DC-area forecast: Hot and humid today before a cooler, wetter weekend
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Mostly sunny early, with clouds increasing later today as highs reach the mid-80s to near 90 — probably our last real taste of summer warmth for the year. A late-day shower or storm is possible, especially in western parts of the area.

What's next? Chances increase this evening for showers and a storm or two with a downpour. A cold front ushers in a much cooler, unsettled weekend pattern with showers or periods of rain at times. Drying out and turning genuinely fall-like early to midweek.

Today's daily digit — 6/10: Hot and humid, with increasing clouds and a late-day storm risk knocking the digit back from Thursday levels. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Friday): Mostly sunny in the morning, then increasing clouds filter more and more sunshine during the afternoon. Highs reach the mid-80s to near 90 with rising humidity (afternoon dew points climbing into the mid- to upper 60s) making it feel a bit toastier still. A chance of a shower or storm mainly after 4 p.m. or so, especially in western parts of the area. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: Scattered showers and a few storms become more likely during the evening and into the night as the front pushes through. One or two could bring briefly heavy rain. Humidity drops off late as lows fall into the mid-50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Saturday): Some showers are around to start the morning but should tend to shift south of the Beltway by around noon, perhaps lingering longer in Southern Maryland. Otherwise, it’s cloudy and a bit breezy from the northeast. Highs are held in the 60s. Confidence: Low-Medium

Tomorrow night: A dry evening is possible, but shower odds rise again later in the night as the next wave of moisture arrives. Lows are mainly in the mid-50s to around 60. Confidence: Medium

Sunday: Rain looks like a good bet, with showers or a steady rain likely for at least part of the day. Some uncertainty remains on exact timing, how much falls, and how late into the day it lasts, but confidence is growing that it’s a damp day overall. Highs are only near 60 to the mid-60s. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Sunday night: By evening it should just be a chance of a passing sprinkle. Otherwise mostly cloudy with lows within a few degrees of 55. Confidence: Medium

Skies clear Monday as the front moves offshore. It turns breezy, with highs in the mid-60s to around 70 — genuinely pleasant fall weather. Monday night lows dip to the 40s. Confidence: Medium

Sunny and cool conditions continue Tuesday and Wednesday, with highs in the low to mid-60s Tuesday and mid- to upper 60s Wednesday. Overnight lows drop into the upper 30s to mid-40s — the chilliest nights of the season so far. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for October 2

Record-shattering heat in 2019 pushed temperatures to an incredible 98 degrees—the hottest ever observed in October and a remarkable extension of summer-like conditions.
